sources.title: Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods
sources.type: Author-deposited manuscript; not an inspection of the subsequently published journal body
sources.text_scope: Physical/printed pages 1–11 and 14–16; selected Remarks 4 and 6 on page 12. Assumptions 1–6, equations (2.2)–(2.9), Theorem 1, aggregation table and equations (3.4)–(3.6).
sources.page_number_rule: Physical and printed page numbers coincide.
sources.verified_scope: Absorbing adoption, whole-unit iid sampling, group-time ATT, conditional counterfactual trends, overlap and known anticipation horizon. Identification uses baseline g−delta−1 and never-treated or eligible not-yet-treated comparisons. OR/IPW/DR population formulas are distinct from estimator inference. Event-time aggregation can change cohort composition; fixed-cohort aggregation removes that source of change.
sources.equation_cautions: Eligibility extends through t+delta. Without a never-treated group, effects after the last eligible comparison disappears are unidentified by this theorem. Observed nonadoption through T differs from known nonadoption beyond T. The cumulative calendar aggregation is not generally a convex average. Random sampling is not randomized adoption.
sources.not_adopted: General nuisance-estimation, multiplier-bootstrap, simultaneous-band or repeated-cross-section proofs; appendices and empirical conclusions were not audited.
sources.chapter_use: Group-time ATT, conditional trends, overlap, anticipation-safe baselines and controls, and supported cohort aggregation. The chapter proves its finite-cell identification/remainder/influence results directly.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from frozen bs_author preparation, which root fully read. No new full-document or appendix inspection claimed by chapter author.

sources.title: Estimating Dynamic Treatment Effects in Event Studies with Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
sources.version: arXiv:1804.05785v2, 22 September 2020; PDF creation metadata is 23 September
sources.type: Author-deposited manuscript; not an inspection of the subsequently published journal body
sources.text_scope: Physical/printed pages 6–8, 12–15 and 21–23: assumptions, coefficient decomposition, auxiliary weight regression, interaction-weighted construction and DID representation.
sources.page_number_rule: Physical and printed page numbers coincide.
sources.verified_scope: Cohort-relative-time effects can contaminate coefficients for other relative times, including leads. Interaction-weighted estimates combine supported cohort-specific effects. A last-treated reference cohort is used only before its adoption; always-treated units lack a preperiod. Normalizations and rank matter when all cohorts eventually adopt.
sources.equation_cautions: Page 15 has an impact-period inconsistency: Proposition 3 states l≥0, whereas equation (15) uses l>0 and adjacent prose removes l≤0. Page 8 Assumption 2 excludes only l<0; retain l=0 treatment effects. Its discussion of older Callaway–Sant’Anna drafts does not describe the inspected December v4 anticipation allowance.
sources.not_adopted: Online Appendix B asymptotic proof, general covariate adjustment or simultaneous inference. Page 23 distinguishes its pointwise inference from simultaneous bands.
sources.chapter_use: Contamination of relative-time coefficients under heterogeneity and cohort-specific aggregation. The full original rational regression is independently derived; impact time zero is included explicitly.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from frozen bs_author preparation, which root fully read. No new full-document or appendix inspection claimed by chapter author.

sources.title: Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment Timing
sources.version: Author manuscript dated August 2020 on its cover; PDF metadata 15 August 2020
sources.type: Author-linked public manuscript; distinct from the NBER 2018 and published 2021 versions
sources.text_scope: Physical pages 1–2, 6–9 and 13–14: cover, setup, FWL, pairwise contrasts/weights, Theorem 1 and causal decomposition (14a)–(15b).
sources.page_number_rule: Cover is unnumbered; body printed page equals physical page minus one.
sources.verified_scope: Balanced-panel binary absorbing-treatment TWFE decomposes into two-by-two contrasts with nonnegative comparison weights determined by sample shares and treatment variation. An already-treated comparison subtracts its changing treatment effect, so positive comparison weights do not imply positive weights on every cohort-date effect.
sources.equation_cautions: Equations (10a)–(10g) are the inspected basic regression decomposition, without an added-covariate extension. Its algebra is not a causal identification assumption. Empty groups, constant treatment and zero residual treatment variance need separate treatment. Extracted mathematical glyphs were unreliable; rendered equations were checked.
sources.not_adopted: Appendix A general proof, empirical estimates or unrestricted extensions. NBER PDF retrieval returned 403; its landing metadata was not substituted for body inspection.
sources.chapter_use: Comparison versus treatment-effect weighting in a basic balanced absorbing-treatment TWFE regression. The chapter proves only its complete original three-cohort/four-date decomposition, not the general appendix theorem.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from frozen bs_author preparation, which root fully read. No new full-document or appendix inspection claimed by chapter author.

sources.title: A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends
sources.version: Published Review of Economic Studies 90(5), 2023, pages 2555–2591; advance access 15 February 2023; DOI 10.1093/restud/rdad018
sources.type: Published journal PDF hosted on an author's website, although the listing link is labeled Draft
sources.text_scope: Physical pages 1–12 / printed 2555–2566: setup, identified set, restriction families, inferential goal and start of moment-inequality representation.
sources.page_number_rule: Printed page equals physical page plus 2554; physical page 1 confirms published identity.
sources.verified_scope: The reduced form separates treatment effects from counterfactual trend departures, with zero pre-treatment effects. Restrictions on departures identify a set. Relative-magnitude restrictions bound consecutive first differences; smoothness bounds second differences. Zero smoothness permits a linear differential trend. Identified sets and confidence sets address different uncertainty.
sources.equation_cautions: Normalize delta_0=0 and justify the reduced form first. Do not treat contaminated raw TWFE leads as clean pretrend departures. Generic closed-convex endpoint language in Lemma 2.1 needs attainment qualifications; the independent caution below supplies them. No pretest proves the missing counterfactual.
sources.not_adopted: General uniform-inference, ARP conditional-testing, power, FLCI or software guarantees. Their later proofs and supplementary material were not inspected.
sources.chapter_use: Reduced-form/departure decomposition, relative-increment versus curvature sensitivity, and the difference between identified and confidence sets. Compact fibers and original square sharpness are proved directly, as is a separate finite known-Gaussian projection.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from frozen bs_author preparation, which root fully read. No new full-document or appendix inspection claimed by chapter author.

cautions_applied: Adoption sampling is not random assignment. Complete iid unit vectors do not justify treating a fixed number of policy clusters as large.
Use baseline g−a−1 and eligible control adoption strictly after t+a. Observed nonadoption through T does not certify no anticipation at t when t+a>T.
The DR population functional uses actual treated share pi for both terms. Normalized true odds are proved separately; no remainder claimed under arbitrary renormalization of misspecified odds.
Retain impact relative time zero. The inspected Sun–Abraham version has an inconsistent impact-period exclusion in one display; no such exclusion is copied.
Finite regression design, normalization, full residual Gram and every outcome-operator entry are explicit. No general all-design decomposition or inference appendix is claimed proved.
Attained sensitivity bounds are proved for nonempty compact convex fibers, with explicit square parametrizations. Closed convexity alone is not taken as a general attainment theorem.
The Gaussian confidence projection includes preperiod uncertainty and is a proved finite stipulated law, not generic uniform asymptotic, ARP, FLCI or bootstrap inference.
not_inspected_or_adopted: NBER Goodman-Bacon PDF returned 403. The author-linked August 2020 public PDF was successfully read instead, and its different version is explicit.
The published Callaway–Sant’Anna, Sun–Abraham and Goodman-Bacon bodies were not inspected; their author versions are the actual equation sources.
Rambachan–Roth later inference proofs and supplementary material, and the other papers' general inference appendices, are outside this scoped reading.
limits: Original examples and solutions are not source empirical tables, current policy estimates, a full-paper proof audit, a validated causal design or external human certification.
